8. It is mentioned in the Writ Petition that petitioner had given an application for obtaining a financial grant from the Government of Madhya Pradesh under Sikshit Berozgar Yojana and accordingly, Collector, District Khandwa granted an amount of Rs.7,000/- to the petitioner i.e. 10%
of the invoice value for purchasing a vehicle.

Petitioner entered into a contract to purchase a motor vehicle Matador for Rs.70,000/- from Harban Singh S/o Amrik Singh and obtained a loan from State Bank of India, Khandwa on the hire purchase basis.

In accordance with the scheme, an amount of Rs.14,000/- i.e. Rs.7,000/- share of the State Government and Rs.7,000/- by the petitioner was deposited in the State Bank of India, Khandwa Branch and accordingly, loan of Rs.56,000/- was approved by the Bank.
On completion of loan process, petitioner got the registration of vehicle done and took the vehicle in possession and certificate of registration of vehicle was also issued.
One Mangilal, who was working in the Fisheries Department, Maheshwar came to Badwah and approached Sharma mechanic and enquired about a vehicle as he wanted to take it on rent.
Thereafter, Sharma mechanic took a room on rent in Atmanand Lodge, Budhwara Bazar.
On 25/12/1981, Mangilal enquired about the address of the petitioner and met with the petitioner.
After introducing himself, he hired the vehicle of the petitioner for attaching in Fisheries Department, Maheshwar for discharge of official work at the rate of Rs.200/- per day.
It was verbally agreed upon that the expenses of driver and diesel of the vehicle would be borne by the Fisheries Department.

On 27/12/1981, vehicle could not be sent to Maheshwar on account of breakdown and on 28/12/1981, petitioner himself took the vehicle and parked at a place informed by Mangilal and petitioner also slept at Mangilal's house.
On 29/12/1981, Mangilal took the documents of the vehicle from his colleague Dr. Devi Singh and reached the office of Fisheries Department to get the complete information about the vehicle.

At the insistence of Mangilal,
petitioner went back to Khandwa and came back on 03/01/1982 to Maheshwar.

In meanwhile,
Mangilal conspired and with an intention to cheat the petitioner committed a fraud and forged the agreement/ sale letter/ power of attorney in the name of Surjan Singh elder brother of Dr. Devi Singh.
Dr. Devi Singh gave Rs.9,000/- as rent of vehicle for one and half months and sent the petitioner back to Khandwa.
Thereafter petitioner was falsely implicated in a case under Section 395 of IPC which was registered at Police Station Karhi, District Khargone.
Petitioner was convicted and he was directed to hand-over the possession of the vehicle in question to Shailendra Singh.
Due to false and fabricated case, petitioner came to Mhow from Khandwa in search of his livelihood leaving behind his mother in Khandwa.
Petitioner's mother died due to an accident in Akola-Indore train at 3 o'clock in the night.
The elder son of petitioner namely, Pradeep also died on account of drowning in the Well.

Thus the petition is filed for a declaration that the petitioner be declared as absolute owner of the vehicle and he is entitled for possession of the same and for payment of compensation amounting to Rs.2,00,00,000/- for undue loss caused by malicious acts of the respondents.

9. Considered the submissions made in the Writ Petition.
10.

Although in paragraph 5.5 of the Writ Petition, it has been mentioned that the petitioner was convicted but for the reasons best known to the petitioner, he has not filed the copy of judgment passed by the Trial Court.

sentences.text: Whether petitioner is the owner of the vehicle in question or not, cannot be decided in a Writ Petition filed under Article 226 of Constitution of India.
When the price of vehicle was only Rs.70,000/-, then how the petitioner has suffered loss of Rs.2,00,00,000/- has also not been clarified.
Even otherwise, quantum of compensation is also a disputed question of fact which cannot be decided in a Writ Petition.
12. Considering the totality of facts and circumstances of the case, this Court is of considered opinion that this petition is misconceived and accordingly, it is dismissed.

(G.S. AHLUWALIA) JUDGE S.M.
